question: A patient presents with intensely itchy papules and excoriations. Which finding, if present, would be pathognomonic of scabies?

answers.text: A short, serpiginous grey line (burrow) in the finger web spaces

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The burrow — a short, grey, serpiginous line created by the female Sarcoptes scabiei tunnelling through the stratum corneum — is the only pathognomonic lesion of scabies. Its predilection for thin-skinned sites such as the finger web spaces, flexor wrists, and genitalia is a key diagnostic clue.

answers.text: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the extensor surfaces

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over extensor surfaces suggest dermatitis herpetiformis, which is associated with coeliac disease. The pathognomonic lesion of scabies is the burrow, found characteristically in web spaces and wrists.

answers.text: Annular scaly plaques with central clearing on the trunk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Annular scaly plaques with central clearing describe tinea corporis (ringworm), a superficial dermatophyte infection. Scabies is identified by its pathognomonic burrows, not annular plaques.

answers.text: Excoriated papules confined to the antecubital and popliteal fossae

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Excoriated papules confined to the antecubital and popliteal fossae suggest atopic dermatitis, which favours these flexural sites. Scabies characteristically spares the flexures and instead affects the web spaces, wrists, periumbilical area, and genitalia.

overallFeedback.feedback: The burrow — a short, grey, serpiginous line in the stratum corneum — is the pathognomonic lesion of scabies. Remember its predilection sites: finger web spaces, flexor wrists, elbows, axillary folds, periumbilical skin, buttocks, and genitalia.
The burrow is the only pathognomonic sign of scabies — always look for it in the web spaces, flexor wrists, periumbilical area, and genitalia when you suspect the diagnosis.
